paragraphs.title: The Destruction and Crisis at Ziklag

answers: The Amalekites
The Philistines
The men of Judah
easy.explanation: The Amalekites invaded Ziklag, smote it, and burned it with fire.

answers: Only the soldiers
The women, sons, and daughters
Only the elders
easy.explanation: The Amalekites carried away the women, sons, and daughters as captives.
easy.q: Whom did the Amalekites take captive?

answers: They immediately went to battle
They returned to Egypt
They wept until they had no more power to weep
easy.explanation: David and the people lifted up their voices and wept until they could weep no more.
easy.q: What did David and his men do when they saw the destruction?

answers: The people spoke of stoning him
He could not find the ephod
His men had left the city
medium.explanation: The people were grieved and spoke of stoning David.

answers: He strengthened his heart by trusting in God
He left the city secretly
He gathered more soldiers from Judah
medium.explanation: David strengthened himself in the LORD before seeking direction.
medium.q: In the KJV, what does “encouraged himself in the LORD” mean in context?

answers: A sword
The ephod
A loaf of bread
medium.explanation: David asked Abiathar to bring the ephod so that he could enquire of the LORD.
medium.q: What did David ask Abiathar to bring him?

answers: He changes from a distressed leader into one who seeks God’s direction and acts
He changes from a victorious warrior into a fugitive
He changes from a wealthy man into a poor man
challenge.explanation: David moves from grief and danger to strengthening himself in the LORD and seeking guidance.
challenge.q: What major change takes place in David during this passage?

answers: The city was burned with fire
They slew not any
The people wept
challenge.explanation: The KJV explicitly says, “they slew not any.”
challenge.q: Which detail shows that the Amalekites took the people captive but did not kill them?

answers: It shows that he sought God’s direction instead of acting only from fear or anger
It proves that the Amalekites had already been defeated
It was a way to choose a new king
challenge.explanation: Although David was under great pressure, he asked the LORD before beginning the pursuit.
challenge.q: Why was David’s enquiry of the LORD important after the people threatened him?

paragraphs.title: The Pursuit and the Abandoned Egyptian

answers: Four hundred
Six hundred
Two hundred
easy.explanation: David went with the six hundred men who were with him.
easy.q: How many men went with David at the beginning of the pursuit?

answers: Two hundred
Four hundred
Six hundred
easy.explanation: Two hundred men stayed behind because they were too faint to cross the brook.
easy.q: How many men remained at the brook Besor?

answers: A sword and a shield
Bread, water, figs, and raisins
Money and clothing
easy.explanation: They gave him bread, water, a piece of a cake of figs, and two clusters of raisins.
easy.q: What did David’s men give the Egyptian?

answers: He had been wounded in battle
He had eaten no bread and drunk no water for three days and three nights
He had been in the wilderness for a month
medium.explanation: The Egyptian said that he had not eaten or drunk for three days and three nights.

answers: Too weak and exhausted to continue
Very eager to fight
Hidden from the enemy
medium.explanation: The two hundred men were so weak that they could not go over the brook.
medium.q: In the KJV, what does “faint” mean in the phrase “which were so faint”?

answers: That he would neither kill him nor deliver him to his master
That he would give him all the spoil
That he would immediately return him to Egypt
medium.explanation: The Egyptian required David to swear that he would not kill him or deliver him to his master.
medium.q: What did David promise the Egyptian?

answers: The Egyptian supplied water for the army
The Egyptian led David to the Amalekite company
The Egyptian guarded the brook
challenge.explanation: After being cared for, the Egyptian agreed to bring David down to the company.
challenge.q: How did caring for the Egyptian help David’s pursuit?

answers: Because the Egyptian received food and water, his spirit came again to him
Because the Egyptian was healthy, he fled from David
Because the men stayed at the brook, they found Ziklag
challenge.explanation: After eating and drinking, the Egyptian recovered his strength.
challenge.q: Which cause-and-effect relationship appears in the passage?

answers: The pursuit was unimportant to him
He showed responsibility toward a weak person even during an urgent pursuit
He intended to return the Egyptian to the Amalekites
challenge.explanation: Despite the urgency, David’s men gave the sick man food and water and cared for him.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from David’s stopping to care for the Egyptian?

paragraphs.title: Victory and Rescue of the Captives

answers: They were arranged in a defensive formation
They were eating, drinking, and dancing over the spoil
They were asking David for peace
easy.explanation: The Amalekites were spread abroad, eating, drinking, and dancing because of the great spoil.
easy.q: What were the Amalekites doing when David found them?

answers: Two hundred
Six hundred
Four hundred
easy.explanation: Four hundred young men escaped on camels.
easy.q: How many young Amalekite men escaped?

answers: Only the sheep
All the captives and the spoil that had been taken
Only his two wives
easy.explanation: David recovered all that the Amalekites had carried away, including the captives and spoil.
easy.q: What did David recover from the Amalekites?

answers: They were scattered and celebrating without a defensive formation
There were very few Amalekites from the beginning
The Amalekites handed over their weapons
medium.explanation: They were spread abroad and celebrating, so they were not prepared for David’s attack.
medium.q: Why was David able to defeat the Amalekites?

answers: A battle from morning until noon
A long period of fighting lasting until the following evening
A battle lasting only one hour
medium.explanation: The phrase describes fighting that continued from twilight until the next evening.
medium.q: What does the phrase “from the twilight even unto the evening of the next day” describe?

answers: Only weapons
Families, flocks, herds, and all the spoil
Only silver and gold
medium.explanation: David recovered the people and the possessions taken by the Amalekites, including flocks and herds.
medium.q: What did the recovered spoil include?

answers: There was nothing lacking, neither small nor great
The Amalekites were dancing
Four hundred men rode upon camels
challenge.explanation: The passage says that nothing was lacking, from sons and daughters to the spoil.
challenge.q: Which detail emphasizes the completeness of the rescue?

answers: The spoil was immediately divided among all the Amalekites
David’s men recognized it as the spoil of David’s victory
David purchased the spoil with money
challenge.explanation: David’s men led the flocks and herds and identified them as David’s spoil.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the words “This is David’s spoil”?

answers: Their celebration left them unprepared for attack
Their celebration caused David to retreat
Their celebration brought them reinforcements
challenge.explanation: They were occupied with eating, drinking, and dancing instead of preparing for defense.
challenge.q: What connection is shown between the Amalekites’ celebration and their defeat?

answers: Two hundred men
Four hundred men
All David’s men
easy.explanation: Two hundred men had remained at the brook because they were too faint to continue.
easy.q: Who remained at the brook Besor?

answers: The opportunity to return to Ziklag
A share of the spoil
The chance to meet David
easy.explanation: They said that the men who had not gone to battle should receive none of the spoil.
easy.q: What did the wicked men want to deny the men who stayed behind?

answers: Only the fighters would receive spoil
The elders of Judah would receive all the spoil
The fighters and those who stayed with the equipment would share alike
easy.explanation: David declared that the fighters and those who tarried by the stuff should have equal parts.

answers: The LORD had preserved them and delivered the enemy into their hand
There was no spoil remaining
The men who stayed behind had fought the most
medium.explanation: David credited the LORD with preserving them and giving them victory.
medium.q: Why did David reject the proposal of the wicked men?

answers: Wicked and worthless men
Wise leaders
Men guarding the equipment
medium.explanation: “Men of Belial” is an expression for wicked or worthless men.
medium.q: In the KJV, what does “men of Belial” describe?

answers: He made it a statute and an ordinance for Israel
He told it only to the elders of Judah
He cancelled it after the battle
medium.explanation: The passage says that David made it a statute and an ordinance for Israel.
medium.q: How did David make his decision a lasting practice?

answers: Only those who fought were true participants
Those who guarded the equipment also contributed and deserved a share
The spoil belonged only to the leader
challenge.explanation: David treated guarding the equipment as an important part of the common effort.
challenge.q: What view of shared responsibility is reflected in David’s decision?

answers: The two groups would receive equal shares
Only the two hundred men would receive spoil
Everyone could take spoil without order
challenge.explanation: David ruled that those who went to battle and those who stayed with the equipment would divide equally.
challenge.q: What does “they shall part alike” mean in context?

answers: It prevented conflict and recognized the contribution of the guards
It allowed the men to hide the spoil
It replaced the fighters with guards
challenge.explanation: Equal sharing reduced division and honored those who protected the supplies.
challenge.q: Why was David’s decision both practical and moral?

paragraphs.title: Gifts to the Elders of Judah

answers: The elders of Judah and his friends
The Amalekites only
The Egyptians only
easy.explanation: David sent gifts to the elders of Judah and to his friends.
easy.q: To whom did David send gifts from the spoil?

answers: A tax from the king
A present from the spoil of the enemies of the LORD
Compensation for the burned city
easy.explanation: David said, “Behold a present for you of the spoil of the enemies of the LORD.”
easy.q: How did David describe the gifts?

answers: Hebron
Ziklag
The brook Besor
easy.explanation: The final verse mentions Hebron and all the places where David and his men were accustomed to go.
easy.q: Which place is mentioned at the end of the list of settlements?

answers: To bless and strengthen his relationships with Judah’s elders and his friends
To purchase weapons from the Amalekites
To return the captives to Egypt
medium.explanation: The gifts were a present from the spoil of the LORD’s enemies to the elders and David’s friends.
medium.q: What was one purpose of David’s gifts?

answers: Property taken from an enemy after victory
A place where people live
A public prayer
medium.explanation: Spoil is property captured from an enemy after a victory.
medium.q: What does “spoil” mean in the phrase “of the spoil of the enemies of the LORD”?

answers: They were sent to one place only
They were sent to many settlements in Judah
They were sent only to the people of Ziklag
medium.explanation: The passage names many places in Judah, ending with Hebron and other places David had visited.
medium.q: What does the list of settlements show about the distribution of the gifts?

answers: They express generosity and shared blessing after the recovery of the spoil
They cancel David’s rule about equal sharing
They punish the elders of Judah
challenge.explanation: After recovering the spoil, David shared part of it with the elders and his friends.
challenge.q: How do the gifts relate to David’s leadership in the chapter?

answers: David and his men had connections with many places where they had stayed or traveled
David had never left Ziklag
All the places were Amalekite camps
challenge.explanation: The wording refers to the many places where David and his men were accustomed to go.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from “all the places where David himself and his men were wont to haunt”?

answers: The spoil is presented as a generous gift, not merely as captured property
The spoil is described as a punishment
The spoil was returned to the Amalekites
challenge.explanation: David presents the captured goods as a blessing and gift from the spoil of the LORD’s enemies.
challenge.q: What is the significance of calling the gift “a present”?

short_answers.question: According to verse 8, what did the LORD promise David he would recover?
short_answers.explanation: The LORD told David to pursue, overtake the enemy, and recover all.

short_answers.question: What did David establish as a statute and ordinance for Israel?
short_answers.answer: That those who went to battle and those who stayed with the equipment should share alike.
short_answers.explanation: David made equal sharing between the two groups a lasting rule.

short_answers.question: To which city did the final verse specifically refer?
short_answers.explanation: The list of places ends with Hebron and all the places where David and his men had been accustomed to go.
